coverageNote: AI stack baseline: 36 definitions across 12 layers. Evidence gaps remain visible. Colors assess narrow documented capabilities, not national AI rankings.

capabilities.name: AI accelerator design
capabilities.definition: Organization-origin accelerator IP; does not establish fabrication location.

capabilities.name: Advanced logic fabrication
capabilities.definition: Operating wafer fabrication at 16 nm class or below, physically inside the country.

capabilities.name: HBM manufacturing
capabilities.definition: Physical domestic fabrication and stacking of high-bandwidth memory; headquarters alone do not qualify.

capabilities.name: Advanced AI packaging
capabilities.definition: Domestic 2.5D/3D semiconductor integration; conventional assembly alone does not qualify.

capabilities.name: AI cluster networking
capabilities.definition: Locally developed high-speed accelerator interconnect systems.

capabilities.name: AI power and cooling
capabilities.definition: Documented domestic operation of AI-specific power and liquid-cooling infrastructure.

capabilities.name: Accelerator cloud access
capabilities.definition: Operational accelerator compute services accessible through a national ecosystem; imported GPUs may qualify for access only.

capabilities.name: Large-scale AI computing
capabilities.definition: Documented multi-accelerator training or serving operation; budgets and proposed clusters do not qualify.

capabilities.name: Edge AI deployment stack
capabilities.definition: Locally developed software or chips supporting device-side inference; release is distinct from fleet adoption.

capabilities.name: Public training datasets
capabilities.definition: Locally originated, released datasets for AI training, with access and license scope checked separately.

capabilities.name: Annotation and curation tools
capabilities.definition: Locally originated tools for collecting, labeling or curating AI datasets.

capabilities.name: Multilingual corpora
capabilities.definition: Locally originated language datasets spanning multiple languages; not a claim to ownership of those languages.

capabilities.name: Foundation-model training
capabilities.definition: Documented original pre-training by organizations originating in the country; fine-tuning alone is insufficient.

capabilities.name: Reasoning and post-training
capabilities.definition: Released reasoning models or documented reinforcement-learning/post-training research.

capabilities.name: Open-weight models
capabilities.definition: Downloadable model weights; open weights do not imply unrestricted licenses or fully open training data.

capabilities.name: Speech and translation
capabilities.definition: Locally originated speech recognition, synthesis or multilingual translation models.

capabilities.name: Vision and multimodal AI
capabilities.definition: Locally originated released vision-language or document-understanding models.

capabilities.name: Image and video generation
capabilities.definition: Locally originated generative image/video model releases; recognition alone does not qualify.

capabilities.name: Training frameworks
capabilities.definition: Locally originated general training frameworks; global contributors and foreign adoption remain separate.

capabilities.name: Distributed training
capabilities.definition: Documented multi-device training software or original training-system engineering.

capabilities.name: Inference runtimes
capabilities.definition: Locally originated runtime, kernel or serving optimization implementations.

capabilities.name: Model API services
capabilities.definition: Operational model-serving APIs from locally originated providers; underlying hardware origin is separate.

capabilities.name: Embeddings and retrieval
capabilities.definition: Locally originated embedding, ranking or retrieval software/models for RAG.

capabilities.name: MLOps and observability
capabilities.definition: Locally originated tools for model lifecycle tracking, evaluation, monitoring or deployment operations.

capabilities.name: Agent frameworks
capabilities.definition: Locally originated released agent orchestration or tool-use implementations; not proof of autonomous reliability.

capabilities.name: Deployed AI applications
capabilities.definition: Named operational AI products; no inference about national adoption or commercial success.

capabilities.name: Embodied AI and robotics
capabilities.definition: Released AI robot-policy or embodied-simulation systems; demonstration is distinct from industrial fleet deployment.

capabilities.name: Evaluation benchmarks
capabilities.definition: Locally originated public evaluation suites, datasets or reproducible harnesses.

capabilities.name: Safety evaluation
capabilities.definition: Published technical risk-testing methods or implementation; policy alone does not establish test execution.

capabilities.name: AI security tooling
capabilities.definition: Released tools specifically testing AI vulnerabilities; general cybersecurity does not qualify.

capabilities.name: Research institutions and talent
capabilities.definition: Named institutions producing original AI research; not a national workforce estimate.

capabilities.name: Open-source AI community
capabilities.definition: Public locally originated AI projects; international contributions do not imply exclusive national ownership.

capabilities.name: AI commercialization
capabilities.definition: Operational AI product providers; financing announcements alone do not establish sales or profitability.

capabilities.name: Published AI governance
capabilities.definition: Published governmental AI governance instruments; maturity measures publication, not policy quality or compliance.

capabilities.name: Public-sector AI deployment
capabilities.definition: Named operational publicly supported AI service; a planned mission alone does not qualify.

capabilities.name: AI standards and interoperability
capabilities.definition: Published public technical frameworks or implementation guidance; not a completeness assessment of national standards.

stageCriteria: 0 — No qualifying evidence entered for the exact definition. Never interpret this as proof of absence.
1 — Documented research or limited demonstration; no usable release or operational service established.
2 — Research implementation, pilot, early deployment or bounded demonstration; operational scale unestablished.
3 — Released usable implementation or documented operational capability within the stated scope. This does not imply widespread adoption, frontier leadership or self-sufficiency.

4 — Primary evidence establishes repeated production/deployment at meaningful scale. A benchmark score, budget, announcement or software repository alone cannot establish this stage. No stage-4 claims are made in this baseline.
researchMethod: Manually reviewed primary-source baseline. Software/model/IP attribution follows originating organization, with global contributions acknowledged. Physical fabrication/packaging/infrastructure require in-country operations. Compute access can rely on imported hardware. All records enter knowledge history on the review date; older publication dates are not fabricated historical assessment dates. Missing quantities and dependencies remain null/unassessed. No automated daily research or national score is claimed.
